title: Location Prepositions
description: Prepositions в and на for location and direction
descriptionRussian: Предлоги в и на для обозначения места и направления
intro: Russian uses two main prepositions for location: в (in) and на (on/at). The tricky part is that the same preposition can mean different things depending on the case that follows. В/на + prepositional case = location (where?). В/на + accusative case = direction (where to?). Some places always use на even when в seems more logical - these must be memorized.
rules: В + prepositional = inside a place: Я в доме. (I'm in the house.)
На + prepositional = on/at a place: Книга на столе. (The book is on the table.)
В + accusative = direction into: Я иду в магазин. (I'm going to the store.)
На + accusative = direction onto: Я иду на работу. (I'm going to work.)
Some places always use на: на работе (at work), на улице (outside), на вокзале (at the station), на почте (at the post office).
examples: Я живу в Москве. (I live in Moscow.), в + prepositional (location)
Я еду в Москву. (I'm going to Moscow.), в + accusative (direction)
Она на работе. (She's at work.), на + prepositional (location)
Она идёт на работу. (She's going to work.), на + accusative (direction)

items.explanation: Use в for being inside cities, buildings, countries: в Москве.

items.promptEnglish: The book is on the table.
items.explanation: Use на for surfaces: на столе (on the table).
Work (работа) always uses на: на работе, на работу.
Use в + accusative for direction into a place: в магазин.
Улица (street/outside) always uses на: на улице.
Вокзал (station) always uses на: на вокзал, на вокзале.
